title: Rav Yehudah of Hagronia
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says he is mentioned once, in Avodah Zarah 39a: Chanan the tailor bought tekhelet (blue dye) from the members of the household of Rabbanai, the brother of R-Ch bar Abba. He came before Rav Matna, who did not have [a ruling] at hand. He came before Rav Yehudah of Hagronia, who said to him, "You have fallen into my hand" ("now you need me," Rashi); thus said Shmuel. Hyman says Yuchasin did not cite this, while Yuchasin HaShalem mentions it under "Chanan." Hyman considers it more likely to follow the reading of R-G, that Chanan came before Rav Yehudah (the student of Shmuel) and [he] said to him, "From Hagronia it fell into [my] hand." See there.

notes.text: The abbreviation ר״ג remains unexpanded. Hyman contrasts נפלת ליד, “you have fallen into my hand,” with מהגרוניא נפלה ליד, “from Hagronia it fell into [my] hand.” In the latter reading, “from Hagronia” belongs to the statement rather than identifying a separate sage. The final speaker remains implicit in Hyman’s wording.

Avodah Zarah 39a gives Rav Yehudah of Hagronia and “you have fallen into my hand.” Rashi explains the clause as “now you need me.” The consulted London and Edinburgh Yuchasin HaShalem (1857), under Chanan the tailor on p. 143, has Rav Yehudah of Hagronia giving the ruling about the wife of a chaver. Hyman (vol. II, p. 616) prefers the alternative in which “from Hagronia” is part of what was said, citing ר״ג. The abbreviation, that alternative witness, and the exact shorter Yuchasin edition behind Hyman’s comparison remain unverified. A separate reading in Rabbeinu Chananel has plain Rav Yehudah, then מתגרניא נפלת ליד in the speech. His gloss understands the term as “one given to quarrelling.” This resembles Hyman’s placement of the word within the speech, while the verb and interpretation differ.
